payload.instructions:
You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>

<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. 2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.

JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

export function parseCSV(text) { return text.trim().split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean).map(line=>line.split(',')); }
export function stringifyCSV(rows) { return rows.map(row=>row.join(',')).join('\r\n'); }

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

anyOf.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default: 1000)

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

tools.name: ci_status
tools.description: Retrieve all current source-revision statuses and new completed CI results in one efficient call. Default cursor advances after retrieval; optional sinceSeq rereads older results.

tools.name: ci_wait
tools.description: Wait for new CI results for up to 60 seconds. Use only when useful independent coding or testing work is exhausted. Returns all current statuses and new results.

tools.name: notifications_dismiss
tools.description: Remove notification IDs together, or use ids:["*"] to remove all active notifications in this session at execution time. Retain them in history.

tools.name: notifications_history
tools.description: Retrieve previously received notifications, including dismissed entries. since is a duration like 2h.

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

anyOf.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default: 1000)

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

tools.name: ci_status
tools.description: Retrieve all current source-revision statuses and new completed CI results in one efficient call. Default cursor advances after retrieval; optional sinceSeq rereads older results.

tools.name: ci_wait
tools.description: Wait for new CI results for up to 60 seconds. Use only when useful independent coding or testing work is exhausted. Returns all current statuses and new results.

tools.name: notifications_dismiss
tools.description: Remove notification IDs together, or use ids:["*"] to remove all active notifications in this session at execution time. Retain them in history.

tools.name: notifications_history
tools.description: Retrieve previously received notifications, including dismissed entries. since is a duration like 2h.

payload.instructions:
You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>

<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

anyOf.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default: 1000)

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

tools.name: ci_status
tools.description: Retrieve all current source-revision statuses and new completed CI results in one efficient call. Default cursor advances after retrieval; optional sinceSeq rereads older results.

tools.name: ci_wait
tools.description: Wait for new CI results for up to 60 seconds. Use only when useful independent coding or testing work is exhausted. Returns all current statuses and new results.

tools.name: notifications_dismiss
tools.description: Remove notification IDs together, or use ids:["*"] to remove all active notifications in this session at execution time. Retain them in history.

tools.name: notifications_history
tools.description: Retrieve previously received notifications, including dismissed entries. since is a duration like 2h.

payload.instructions:
You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>

<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.

Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.

For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

anyOf.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of results (default: 1000)

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

path.description: Directory to list (default: current directory)

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

tools.name: ci_wait

tools.name: notifications_dismiss

tools.name: notifications_history

payload.instructions:
You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.

<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- grep: Search file contents for patterns (respects .gitignore)
- find: Find files by glob pattern (respects .gitignore)
- ls: List directory contents

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>

<rules>
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.

Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit

# Package Catalog

Complete this dependency-free Node 24 application. Existing CSV, version and catalog helpers require regression acceptance from background CI. Implement useful features while CI runs. Keep implementation in src as .mjs modules with literal relative import paths; additional helpers are allowed. Do not change this specification, package.json or existing test files; add your own tests and usage documentation in new files.

## Existing contracts

`src/csv.mjs` exports `parseCSV(text)` and `stringifyCSV(rows)`. RFC4180-style comma-separated rows, quoted commas, escaped double quotes, CRLF/LF and newlines inside quoted fields must round-trip. Empty input yields []; a final record separator adds no empty record. Preserve spaces. Reject unclosed quotes and quotes in unquoted fields. Every value is a string.

`src/version.mjs` exports `parseVersion(text)` and `compareVersions(a,b)`. Versions have exactly three nonnegative integer components with no leading zero except zero. Optional prerelease components contain ASCII alphanumerics/hyphens, separated by dots; numeric components reject leading zero. No build metadata. Parsed form is `{major,minor,patch,prerelease:[string,...]}`. Compare numerically; release beats prerelease; numeric prerelease is below alphabetic, numeric values compare numerically, otherwise ASCII ordering; shorter identical prefix is lower. Return -1,0,1. Reject invalid versions.

`src/catalog.mjs` exports `createCatalog(seed=[])`. A record is `{id,name,version,tags,dependencies}`: nonempty string id/name, valid version, string tags, dependency id strings. Trim id/name, normalize tags to lowercase trimmed unique sorted values (discard empty tags); preserve dependency order but remove duplicates. Store/return independent deep copies. Methods: `list()`, `get(id)` (null absent), `add(record)` (reject duplicate id), `update(id,patch)` (reject absent/id changes), `remove(id)` (boolean), `applyBatch(operations)` (add/update/remove objects; all-or-nothing transaction). Reject malformed operations/records; unknown dependency ids are allowed at storage time. List by id using ASCII order. Failed writes leave all state unchanged.

## Features to build

1. `src/search.mjs`: `searchRecords(records,query={})` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Case-insensitive trimmed `text` matches name OR id; `tags` require ALL normalized tags; `versionMin`/`versionMax` inclusive semantic version bounds; `sortBy` id/name/version, `order` asc/desc, default id asc; always break ties by id ascending. Default offset 0, limit 20; integers offset>=0, 1<=limit<=100. Reject invalid sort/order/paging; do not mutate inputs.
2. `src/graph.mjs`: `planDependencies(records,requestedIds)` returns dependency-first unique ids. Process requested ids in input order and each node's dependencies in stored order; DFS postorder. Reject missing ids and cycles, with an error mentioning missing id or cycle ids. `reverseDependencies(records,id)` returns sorted ids that transitively depend on id; excludes id; reject unknown id. Do not mutate inputs.
3. `src/transfer.mjs`: `exportCSV(records)` header exactly `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`; tags/dependencies pipe-joined. `importCSV(text,catalog)` parses/validates whole input then atomically adds all records; exact header required, duplicate ids reject, return added records. `exportNDJSON(records)` yields an async iterator of JSON string plus newline per record. `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` accepts async string/Buffer chunks with UTF-8 characters possibly split across Buffer boundaries, empty lines ignored, final line without newline allowed. Validate atomically; malformed JSON or record leaves catalog unchanged; return added records.
4. `src/server.mjs`: export `createServer(catalog)` returning an unlistening node:http Server. JSON HTTP endpoints: GET /health ->200 `{ok:true}`; GET /records with text, tags comma-separated, versionMin/Max, sortBy, order, offset, limit -> search response; POST /records JSON ->201 created; GET /records/:id ->200 record; PATCH ->200 updated; DELETE ->204; GET /plan?ids=a,b ->200 `{ids:[...]}`; GET /export.csv ->200 text/csv; POST /import.csv ->201 `{added:N}`; POST /import.ndjson ->201 `{added:N}`; GET /export.ndjson ->200 application/x-ndjson. Unknown route/id404, malformed input400 with JSON `{error:string}`, duplicate creation409. Limit request bodies to 1 MiB; oversize413. URL-decode ids. No unhandled rejection or process exit on bad requests.
5. `src/cli.mjs`: runnable `node src/cli.mjs <command> --file <JSON file> ...`. Commands list (JSON search envelope; optional --text, --tags), add (record from --record JSON), remove (--id), plan (--ids comma-separated), import-csv (--input path), export-csv. File is a JSON array, absent file starts empty. Writes use temporary file + rename only after full validation. Output JSON except export-csv; invalid input exits nonzero with stderr and leaves data untouched. --file is mandatory.
6. Add meaningful regression tests and `USAGE.md` covering HTTP, CLI, CSV/NDJSON and errors. All functionality must work together.

CI automatically snapshots watched source files and executes tests in background. Results are external observations tied to a job id and source revision. A failed old snapshot does not imply current code is still wrong. Check current revisions; finish only after the latest CI jobs have passed and your full tests pass. Continue independent useful work between CI checks. Wait for a result only after useful independent work is exhausted.

{"path":"USAGE.md","content":"# Package Catalog usage

Requires Node 24; no dependencies to install. Run `npm test` for all local tests.

## Records and modules

Records contain `id`, `name`, `version`, `tags` (string array), and `dependencies` (id array). For example:

```json
{"id":"web","name":"Web Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}
```

Ids/names are trimmed; tags are trimmed, lowercased, deduplicated and sorted. Dependencies retain their order without duplicates. Versions use three integer components and optional prerelease, not build metadata. Unknown dependency ids can be stored, but dependency planning rejects missing nodes and cycles.

`createCatalog` from `src/catalog.mjs` stores independent copies and supports atomic `applyBatch` operations (`{type:'add',record}`, `{type:'update',id,patch}`, `{type:'remove',id}`). Search and graph helpers never mutate inputs. Search defaults to id ascending, offset 0, limit 20; limits must be 1–100. Sorting ties always use id ascending. Dependency plans use dependency-first DFS order; reverse dependencies are sorted transitively.

## HTTP

Start an empty in-memory catalog with `npm start` (default port 3000, configurable using `PORT`). Data is not persisted by this server. Embedding applications may import `createServer(catalog)` from `src/server.mjs` and call `.listen()` themselves.

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/health
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/records \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"web","name":"Web Tools","version":"1.2.0","tags":["tools"],"dependencies":[]}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/records?text=web&tags=tools&versionMin=1.0.0&sortBy=version&order=desc&offset=0&limit=20'
curl http://localhost:3000/records/web
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:3000/records/web -d '{"name":"Updated Tools"}'
curl 'http://localhost:3000/plan?ids=web'
curl -X DELETE http://localhost:3000/records/web
```

GET `/records` returns `{items,total,offset,limit}`. Text matches id or name case-insensitively; all comma-separated tags must match; `versionMin` and `versionMax` are inclusive. `sortBy` accepts id/name/version and `order` asc/desc. GET `/plan` returns `{ids:[...]}`. Percent-encode ids in `/records/:id` (including embedded slashes).

Creation returns 201, reads/updates 200, deletion 204. Unknown routes or record ids return 404, duplicate creation 409, malformed input 400, and bodies above 1 MiB 413. Error bodies are JSON `{error:string}`. Failed writes/imports leave the catalog unchanged.

## CLI persistence

Every command requires `--file`; its contents must be a JSON array. A nonexistent file begins empty. Mutation commands validate fully before writing a same-directory temporary file and renaming it over the destination. Read-only commands do not create an absent file. This is single-writer persistence, not concurrent-write coordination.

```sh
node src/cli.mjs list --file catalog.json --text web --tags tools,web
node src/cli.mjs add --file catalog.json --record '{"id":"web","name":"Web","version":"1.0.0","tags":[],"dependencies":[]}'
node src/cli.mjs plan --file catalog.json --ids web
node src/cli.mjs remove --file catalog.json --id web
node src/cli.mjs import-csv --file catalog.json --input packages.csv
node src/cli.mjs export-csv --file catalog.json > packages.csv
```

Output is JSON except for `export-csv`. Remove returns a boolean; import returns `{added:N}`. Invalid options, records, files or dependency plans emit stderr and exit nonzero without altering stored data.

## CSV and NDJSON

```sh
curl http://localhost:3000/export.csv > packages.csv
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.csv --data-binary @packages.csv
curl http://localhost:3000/export.ndjson > packages.ndjson
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/import.ndjson --data-binary @packages.ndjson
```

CSV requires the exact header `id,name,version,tags,dependencies`. Tags and dependencies are pipe-separated; an empty cell means an empty array. Quoted commas, doubled quotes, embedded newlines and CRLF/LF are supported; whitespace is preserved by the CSV parser. The pipe-delimited format has no escaping for literal pipes inside tags or dependency ids; use NDJSON for those values.

`src/transfer.mjs` exports `exportCSV(records)`, `importCSV(text,catalog)`, `exportNDJSON(records)` (async iterator of newline-terminated JSON strings), and `importNDJSON(chunks,catalog)` (async iterable of strings/Buffers). NDJSON accepts split UTF-8 Buffer characters, blank lines, and a final line without a newline. HTTP export content types are `text/csv` and `application/x-ndjson`; imports return 201 `{added:N}`. Both import formats add records, never replace them, and validate the whole input atomically. Bad headers, JSON, records, or duplicate ids leave all existing records untouched.
"}

tools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

anyOf.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)
Maximum number of lines to read

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

pattern.description: Search pattern (regex or literal string)

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

tools.name: find
tools.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

tools.description: Retrieve all current source-revision statuses and new completed CI results in one efficient call. Default cursor advances after retrieval; optional sinceSeq rereads older results.

tools.description: Retrieve previously received notifications, including dismissed entries. since is a duration like 2h.
